text:
Aiden: Heads-up — saw a cascade in the proxy nodepool (eu-west-1) after yesterday's infra patch. Autoscaler spun up 6 nodes, a bunch of proxy pods scheduled on them, then immediately started scale-down and we ended up with Pending GPU workloads. Logs attached.
Priya: Yikes. Any reason scale-down kicked in so fast? Last I checked we had a 10m unneeded-time set.
Aiden: root cause looks like a mix: small init-proxy DaemonSet + hostPath logging causing nodes to be considered "not empty" and some preemptible spot churn. CA saw nodes as underutilized after pods moved and triggered down.
Marco: Can we reproduce locally with a nodepool of 1 preemptible + 2 regular and a few small pods with hostPath? I suspect skip-nodes-with-local-storage is preventing removal.
Elena: Also saw a lot of pod re-scheduling due to proxy init ordering — services hit external NATs and some AZs ran out of ephemeral IPs, causing startup retries. That made utilisation look low for a few minutes.
Priya: Quick mitigation: temporarily bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m and --scale-down-delay-after-add to 30m. Also toggle --expander=most-pods so CA prefers nodes that free more pods when scaling up/down.
Aiden: Trying those now on canary cluster. Also setting --max-node-provision-time to 15m to avoid premature scale-down during longer boot.
Marco: For longer term: annotate the proxy DaemonSet with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled? But it's a DaemonSet — maybe better to mark nodes with a dedicated taint and use podAffinity to stick proxies to non-burst pools.
Elena: Agree — we should avoid proxies landing on preemptible/spot-only pools. Add nodeAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution to prefer stable pools.
Priya: We should also identify pods with local storage or hostPath and add annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/expander-priority? There's a risk of over-annotating though.
Aiden: Small debug log from CA: "scale-down: node x considered unneeded; has 2 system pods, skip-nodes-with-system-pods=true". So some system pods are considered movable but hostPath blocked eviction.
Marco: Two follow-ups: 1) check daemonset tolerations — maybe some system pods are marked static. 2) Set --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true (default) but audit which pods actually use hostPath; we can migrate logs to sidecar with PVCs.
Elena: Network angle: opened ticket with cloud for NAT exhaustion in eu-west private subnets. If NAT pools are exhausted, startup backoffs look like evictions because pods fail liveness quickly.
Priya: Cost tradeoff: bumping unneeded-time increases short-term cost. We should only apply to eu-west proxy pool and keep other regions at 10m.
Aiden: Canary applied: --scale-down-unneeded-time=20m --scale-down-delay-after-add=30m --expander=most-pods on autoscaler-deploy/eu-west-proxy. Monitoring.
(ops-bot): Deploy 2149991111: rollout started for autoscaler-eu-west-proxy -> replicas:1
Marco: After 12m, CA didn't scale-down. Good. CPU-based bins stable, no Pending GPUs so far.
Elena: Still seeing a couple of failed proxy init retries due to NAT throttling; cloud says they'll add 50 ephemeral IPs tomorrow.
Priya: Follow-up PR ideas: 1) Add nodeAffinity to proxy DaemonSet to prefer stable-pools 2) Add pod annotation checklist for hostPath usage 3) Update infra-runbook with CA flags per pool.
Aiden: I'll open a ticket with infra-runbook steps and a follow-up to test with --expander=least-waste in staging. For now keep canary flags in eu-west for 24h.
Marco: One more: consider --balance-similar-node-groups=true to reduce cross-group oscillation when AZ hit capacity.
Aiden: Noted. Will include in runbook and schedule a postmortem after 48h if things reoccur.
Elena: Thanks folks :thumbsup:
(ops-bot): Alert cleared 2149991180: proxy nodepool surge resolved, 0 Pending GPUs
